ruleHints.address: IPv4 or IPv6 address; a slash means a subnet (e.g. 192.0.2.0/24). Filling both sides matches source and destination together. A single IP and subnet cannot be combined.
ruleHints.protocol: Ports require all / tcp / udp. icmp_type and icmp_code apply only to icmp / icmpv6; tcp_flags applies only to tcp.
ruleHints.ttl: Use a single value, range, or comma-separated list. Prefix with ! to negate. Examples: 64 · 64,128 · 0-31 · !0-31
ruleHints.pkt_len: Packet length in bytes. Same syntax as ttl, e.g. 64-512.
ruleHints.icmp_type: Applies only to icmp / icmpv6. Same syntax as ttl.
ruleHints.icmp_code: Applies only to icmp / icmpv6. Same syntax as ttl.
ruleHints.fragment: Fragment position: nofrag unfragmented · first first · middle middle · last last · frag any fragment · nonfirst any except first. Separate choices with commas; prefix with ! to negate.
ruleHints.tcp_flags: TCP flags FIN SYN RST PSH ACK URG ECE CWR, separated by commas. Prefix a flag with ! to require it unset. Example: SYN,!ACK. Applies only to tcp.
ruleHints.match_anomaly: Anomalous packet bitmask; add values: 1 bad fragment · 2 invalid packet · 4 length mismatch · 8 IPv4 TCP fragment offset of 1. Requires a specific target address. IPv6 does not support 1 or 8.

ruleErrors.anomalyIPv6: IPv6 addresses do not support match_anomaly values 1 and 8

ruleErrors.fragmentIPv4: fragment requires IPv4 and an address or subnet
ruleErrors.nonfirst: Nonfirst fragments (or match_anomaly 8) have no port header; ports, tcp_flags, or ICMP conditions cannot also be specified

ruleErrors.lengthBoth: New and legacy packet length syntax cannot be combined

ruleErrors.decimal: {value} is not a valid decimal integer
ruleErrors.emptyItem: {key} has an empty item (an extra comma?)
ruleErrors.fragmentName: fragment does not recognize {value}; use nofrag / first / middle / last / frag / nonfirst
ruleErrors.flagName: Unknown TCP flag {value}; use FIN SYN RST PSH ACK URG ECE CWR

settingsUI.writingIntro: One rule per line. Separate field=value pairs with spaces; lines starting with # are comments.
settingsUI.writingTarget: Omit dst_ip / dst_cidr. Choose the targets to protect when importing.
settingsUI.writingProtocol: all / tcp / udp / icmp… (icmp and similar protocols cannot specify ports)
settingsUI.writingFlags: For example SYN,!ACK (! means the bit is unset; tcp only)
settingsUI.writingAction: drop discards / rate_limit limits the rate
settingsUI.writingRate: Packets per second (pps); required for the rate_limit action
settingsUI.writingExpiry: Time until expiry, such as 30m 6h 1h30m; omitted means permanent
settingsUI.exampleRules:
# DNS / NTP reflection: drop UDP from source ports 53 and 123; expires after 6 hours
protocol=udp src_port=53 action=drop expires_in=6h
protocol=udp src_port=123 action=drop expires_in=6h
# SYN flood: limit TCP with SYN set and ACK unset to 50,000 packets per second
protocol=tcp tcp_flags=SYN,!ACK action=rate_limit rate_limit=50000
